title: Cotton vs Rayon vs Silk Kurtis: Which One Should You Choose?
excerpt: Choosing the right fabric for your kurti is important for both comfort and style. Learn about the differences between cotton, rayon, and silk.

content.text: Choosing the right fabric for your kurti is important for both comfort and style. Cotton, rayon, and silk are among the most popular fabrics used in ethnic wear. Each fabric has its own advantages and is suitable for different occasions.
Cotton Kurtis
Cotton kurtis are one of the most comfortable choices, especially for daily wear. Cotton is a natural fabric that allows air circulation and absorbs moisture, making it ideal for hot climates.

title: Best Fabrics for Summer Kurtis in India
excerpt: Indian summers can be extremely hot, so choosing the right fabric is essential for comfort. Discover the best summer fabrics.

content.text: Indian summers can be extremely hot, so choosing the right fabric is essential for comfort. Lightweight and breathable fabrics help keep you cool throughout the day.
Cotton
Cotton is the most popular summer fabric. It is breathable, absorbs sweat, and feels comfortable even in high temperatures.
Linen
Linen is another excellent summer fabric. It allows airflow and keeps the body cool, making it suitable for both casual and semi-formal wear.
Rayon
Rayon is lightweight and soft. It drapes well and feels comfortable, making it a good option for stylish summer kurtis.
Khadi
Khadi is a natural handwoven fabric that is breathable and eco-friendly. It is ideal for those who prefer sustainable fashion.
Conclusion
For Indian summers, cotton and linen kurtis are usually the most comfortable, while rayon provides a stylish alternative for everyday wear.

title: How to Store Ethnic Wear Properly
excerpt: Proper storage helps maintain the quality and longevity of your ethnic wear. Learn the best practices for storing your kurtis.

content.text: Proper storage helps maintain the quality and longevity of your ethnic wear. Kurtis made from delicate fabrics like silk or embroidered materials require extra care.
Clean Before Storing
Always wash or dry clean your clothes before storing them. Dirt or sweat left on fabric can damage it over time.
Use Proper Hangers
Use padded or wooden hangers for kurtis to maintain their shape. Avoid thin wire hangers that may stretch the fabric.
Store in Breathable Covers
For delicate fabrics like silk or embroidered kurtis, use cotton garment bags instead of plastic covers. This allows air circulation and prevents moisture buildup.
Protect from Moisture
Keep your ethnic wear in a dry place. Moisture can cause mold and damage fabrics.
Avoid Direct Sunlight
Sunlight can fade colors over time, so store your kurtis in a cool and shaded area.
Proper storage ensures your ethnic wear remains fresh and beautiful for a long time.
